answer: Appeal-bond ladders resist sybils: disputing or overturning a verdict requires posting a bond that scales with how often the SAME identity has appealed recently, so a swarm spamming appeals faces geometrically rising stakes anchored to its own behavior. A nebula of fakes each filing frivolous disputes burns escalating collateral toward the glacier of ruin; one honest appeal costs the flat floor. The ladder keys to per-identity appeal frequency, so grief-flooding the dispute system prices itself out while genuine single appeals stay cheap.
